input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The new minimum wait defaults to one second instead of zero.
- failure path: With default options, an early exponential result below one second is raised to a one-second delay, slowing retries that previously had no configured floor.

Reviewer finding
- description: The new `min` parameter defaults to 1 second, so existing callers that never pass `min` now get a floor of 1 second where the previous minimum was 0.
- rationale: Trigger: a caller uses wait_exponential_jitter(initial=0.1, max=10) without min. Before this change, the first wait could be about 0.1 seconds. Now the mechanism is max(max(0, self.min), ...) with self.min=1, so every wait is raised to at least 1 second. Impact: existing retry timing changes silently after an upgrade, which can slow retries for users who relied on sub-second backoff.
critique: The finding names the same root cause, a new `min` that defaults to 1 instead of 0. It also traces the same failure path: sub-second exponential waits are clamped up to 1 second for callers using default options.
